title: AO/259/2020 of VIVEK PATHAK Vs SMT. SUMERA PASWAN

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Appeal From Order No. 259 of 2020
Vivek Pathak and another ........... Appellants
Vs.
Smt. Sumera Paswan and others ........ Respondents

Present : Mr. Sudhir Kumar, Advocate for the appellants.
 Mr. Suhaas Ratna Joshi, Advocate for the respondents.
JUDGMENT
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
 Instant appeal is preferred against the
Judgment and Order dated 15.12.2020, passed in Civil
Appeal No.14 of 2018, Nangu (dead) through LRs vs. Smt.
Neena Pathak and others, by the court of District Judge,
Nainital (for short, "the appeal"). By it, the Judgment and
Order dated 05.02.2018, passed in Civil Suit No.97 of
2010, Yagya Prakash Pathak (dead) through LRs vs.
Nangu (for short, "the suit"), passed by the court of Civil
Judge (Sr. Div.), Haldwani, District Nainital has been set
aside. By the Judgment and Order dated 05.02.2018,
passed in the case, the suit filed by the appellant for
permanent injunction has been decreed.
2. Facts necessary to appreciate the controversy
briefly stated are that the appellants and others filed the
suit for permanent injunction with regard to property plot
no.199, 200, 201, 202, 203, 205 of Khata No.147 and

2
148, (the present new revenue numbers are 71, 72, 73,
74, 75, 76, 77) situated in village Haldwani, Malli Pargana
Bhabhar, Tehsil Haldwani, District Nainital (hereinafter
referred as to, "the suit property"). It is the case of the
appellants that this property was purchased by their
predecessors-in-interest through a sale deed on
31.03.1943. They are recorded tenure holder in
possession of the suit property since then. But, the
respondents are trying to interfere in the peaceful
possession of the appellants and others.
3. The suit was decreed on 05.02.2018, against
which, the appeal was preferred. In the appeal, the
appellate court observed that the plot/khasra no.199 is
not recorded in the name of the ancestors of the
appellants and it was also observed that, "on perusal of
impugned judgment, the lower Court miserably failed
to reach a specific conclusion regarding the
Khasra/plot no.199 as mentioned in the plaint
whether the plaintiff has attained the ownership or
possession of the said land. So the matter needs re-consideration after proper re-appreciation of evidence
put forwarded by the parties". While observing so, the
matter was remanded to the lower court to decide it
afresh. This judgment and order dated 15.12.2020,
passed in the appeal is impugned herein.

3
4. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the record.
5. Learned counsel for the appellants would
submit that this order remanding the case is not in
accordance with law. Learned counsel raised the following
points in his submissions:-
(i) The suit property has been recorded in the
name of appellants and other co-sharers.
(ii) The appellants and co-sharers, have
categorically in para 1 of the plaint stated that
they are recorded tenure holders in possession
of the suit property. This fact has not been
specifically denied by the respondents in their
written statement.
(iii) The respondents in their written
statement, in paragraph 7, averred that they
had filed a suit in the revenue court claiming
owner of the suit property and they claim their
ownership on the basis of possession. It
according to the learned counsel, in fact,
impliedly admits that the claim of the
appellants and co-sharers are recorded tenure
holders of the suit property.

4
(iv) Appellants and their co-sharers are,
in fact, recorded tenure holders of the property
and the documents have been filed in the suit.
6. Learned counsel made reference to Order 41 of
the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (for short, "CPC") to
argue that remand of a case may be made by the appellate
court, under Order 41 Rule 23, 23A and 25 CPC, but, it is
argued that in the instant case, none of the provisions is
applicable. Particularly, it is submitted that, in case, the
court from whom, decree and appeal is preferred has
disposed of the case otherwise on the preliminary points,
and the decree is reversed in appeal and a retrial is
considered necessary, in such a situation, remand of the
case may be made under Order 41 Rule 23A CPC.
7. It is submitted that in the instant case, the
decree has not been reversed. Decree is basically formal
expression of the adjudication. The ownership of the suit
property of the appellants, as upheld in the suit, has not
been reversed in the appeal. Therefore, there was no
occasion to remand the case. In support of his contention,
learned counsel placed reliance to the principle of law laid
down in the case of P. Purushottam Reddy and another
vs. Pratap Steels Ltd., (2002) 2 SCC 686. In the case of P.
Purushottam Reddy (supra), the Hon'ble Supreme
Court inter alia held that unless there is specific

5
provision for remand of a case, a case may not be
remanded. It was observed that:-
"In 1976, Rule 23-A has been inserted in Order 41
which provides for a remand by an appellate court
hearing an appeal against a decree if (i) the trial court
disposed of the case otherwise than on a preliminary
point, and (ii) the decree is reversed in appeal and a
retrial is considered necessary. On twin conditions
being satisfied, the appellate court can exercise the
same power of remand under Rule 23-A as it is under
Rule 23. After the amendment, all the cases of
wholesale remand are covered by Rules 23 and 23-A."
8. On the other hand, learned counsel appearing
for the respondents would submit that in the instant case
the issue revolves around ownership of the suit property.
Learned counsel raised the following points:-
(i) The suit property is not mentioned in the
sale deed dated 31.03.1943, on which, the
appellants based their claim.
(ii) Revenue record is not proof of ownership.
It is argued that, in fact, the appellants
manipulated to forge the revenue record. The
respondents had filed a suit in the revenue
court for establishing their title.
9. Who is owner of the suit property? This is not
for adjudication at this stage before this Court. A very
short issue is for consideration i.e. as to whether, the
judgment and order dated 15.12.2020 remanding the case
is, in accordance with law or not? As stated, the case has

6
been remanded on the ground that the trial court did not
record any finding with regard to plot no.199. It may be
stated that plot no.199 is part of the suit property and, in
fact, in the plaint, the appellants have categorically stated
that new numbers of plot no.199 are plot nos.71, 72, 73
and 74.
10. Learned counsel appearing for the appellants
has referred to the findings recorded by the trial court in
the judgment and order dated 05.02.2018. A perusal of
the judgment and order dated 05.02.2018, passed in the
suit, reveals that, categorical finding has been recorded in
it with regard to ownership and possession of the entire
suit property. In paragraphs 17 and 19 of the judgment,
there is great deliberation on this point. At paragraph 17
in page 9, in the judgment and order dated 05.02.2018, it
is categorically recorded that the sale deed and other
documentary evidence proves that the appellants and co-sharers are recorded tenure holders, owner in possession
of the suit property. In fact, at page no.10, bottom lines
and in page no.11 para 19 bottom line of the judgment in
the suit, the documents filed by the respondents and
appellants respectively have been discussed. At page
no.10, bottom lines of the judgment dated 05.02.2018 of
the suit, the court has recorded the finding that the
appellants and their predecessors-in-interest have been

7
recorded Bhumidhars/Khudkhast on the suit property,
which confirms their claim. It was so done while
discussing the documents filed by the respondents. At
page 11, para 19 bottom lines of the judgment in the suit,
the court while discussing the documents filed by the
appellants has held that in the khata and khatoni, the
suit property has been recorded in the name of the
predecessors-in-interest of the appellants and thereafter,
the appellants. Therefore, this Court is of the view that the
finding that the trial court did not record specific
conclusion recorded Khasra/plot no.199, as recorded in
the judgment of the appeal is against record. It requires
interference. In view of it, the appeal deserves to be
allowed.
11. The appeal is allowed. The impugned Judgment
and Order dated 15.12.2020, passed in Civil Appeal No.14
of 2018, Nangu (dead) through LRs vs. Smt. Neena Pathak
and others, by the court of District Judge, Nainital, is set
aside. The appellate court is requested to decide the
appeal afresh in view of the observations made in this
judgment.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 27.10.2021
Sanjay
